Reasoning: Let the widths of the two columns be a and b respectively, and the heights of the two rows be c and d respectively. The sums of the perimeters of two diagonally opposite small rectangles are equal, and both are equal to 2(a+b+c+d), which is the perimeter of the large rectangle WXYZ. It is known that the perimeters of three small rectangles are 11, 16, and 19, the fourth is p, and 11 < p < 19. The four numbers must be able to be divided into two groups of diagonally opposite small rectangles so that the sums of the two groups are equal. Check the pairing: 11+19=30, 16+p must equal 30, so p=14, satisfying 11 < 14 < 19. Therefore the perimeter of the large rectangle is 11+19=30.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a rectangle divided by one vertical segment and one horizontal segment into a 2-by-2 array of four rectangles. Let the column widths be a and b, and the row heights be c and d. Then the four small perimeters are 2(a+c), 2(b+c), 2(a+d), and 2(b+d). From this, opposite small rectangles have perimeters whose sums are both 2(a+b+c+d), which is exactly the perimeter of the large rectangle WXYZ. Use the text-given three perimeters 11, 16, and 19, and let the unknown fourth perimeter be p, with 11 < p < 19. Pair the four numbers so opposite pairs have equal sum: the only possible equal pairing satisfying the interval condition is 11 + 19 = 16 + p, so p = 14 and the large rectangle perimeter is 30.
